prTitle: support Fulfillment Options — FO selection on shipping-option create/update (CMRC-789, CMRC-790)
stackAndServices: TypeScript monorepo: packages/admin/dashboard (React admin UI), packages/medusa (Express-style API routes), packages/modules/fulfillment (module service + provider service), packages/core/core-flows (workflow orchestration, cart checkout flows), packages/core/js-sdk (typed HTTP client), packages/core/types (shared HTTP DTOs). Postgres-backed.
verdictBasis: The one clean discriminating claim the diff supports is: 'an admin who selects a specific Fulfillment Option while creating a shipping option gets a persisted ShippingOption.data that matches that selection (bound to the create-shipping-option user-action window), and this is impossible to produce with an empty/garbage selection because the create form now requires fulfillment_option_id (zod .min(1)).' P'(b) requires this bound to a harness-observed persisted delta AND confirmed on a fresh-session user surface. The persisted-delta leg is satisfiable (DB diff on shipping_option row created inside the action window). The fresh-session leg is NOT satisfiable through the admin UI as shipped: the edit-shipping-option form (edit-shipping-option-form.tsx) had its entire provider_id/fulfillment-option Form.Field block deleted in this same PR, and the list/detail views never render `data` or the chosen FO id anywhere. There is no admin-UI surface, before or after this PR, that displays which Fulfillment Option a shipping option is bound to. The only alternative fresh-session witness is an indirect one — a storefront customer adding that shipping method to a cart during checkout, which triggers validateAndReturnShippingMethodsDataStep -> IFulfillmentModuleService.validateFulfillmentData. I fetched the only CONJURE-able (no vendor creds needed) provider's source, packages/modules/providers/fulfillment-manual/src/services/manual-fulfillment.ts, and confirmed validateFulfillmentData is `async validateFulfillmentData(optionData, data, context) { return data }` — an unconditional passthrough — and validateOption always `return true`. Checkout would succeed identically whether the admin selected the correct FO, a wrong FO, or (pre-PR) no FO at all with empty data. The one available downstream behavioral witness is provably non-discriminating for this feature's core claim in a stock sandbox. With no viable first-leg substitute and no discriminating second leg, P'(b)'s dual-leg bar cannot be honestly cleared -> CND. Confession: I did not stand up the actual sandbox and run the walk; this verdict is a structural prediction from reading the diff plus the manual provider source, which is what the blind protocol asks for. notCovered: whether a first-party fulfillment provider plugin elsewhere in the repo has a non-trivial validator that could legitimately serve as a second leg — I did not exhaustively search third-party provider plugins outside packages/modules/providers/.
holds: Effect-check binding to a harness-observed DB delta on `shipping_option` inside the create-action window is a clean, well-typed target — the row and its `data` column are unambiguous and directly tied to the diff (create-shipping-options-form.tsx now sends `data: fulfillmentOptionData`).
Quantifier lint correctly does not trigger — the intent is per-entity ('this shipping option gets this FO'), no any/all/every language, so FW-11 owner-shadow collapse is not a live risk here.

The theory correctly forces CND rather than a false WORKS on the removed edit-time provider_id control: a hostile class ('can an admin still change providers post-creation via the UI?') has no front-door control to exercise at all post-PR, so it is honestly NOT-EXECUTED -> CND instead of being silently skipped or wrongly marked SURVIVED.

The 'switch provider after picking an option' hostile class is well-specified and front-door-executable: onChange resets fulfillment_option_id to "" and the Select remounts via `key={selectedProviderId}`, so a click-driven repro (pick provider A + option, switch to provider B, attempt submit) should SURVIVE cleanly against a harness DB diff showing zero new rows until re-selection.

The empty-selection hostile class (submit with no FO chosen) is also cleanly front-door-testable and should SURVIVE: zod .min(1) blocks the mutation client-side, so the harness's idle-baseline diff should show no `shipping_option` write at all — a good calibrated-mutation-attribution case (1.2).

breaks.detail: This PR adds a create-time-only admin control (Fulfillment Option Select) with no corresponding show/edit-time UI surface for the same field — it actively deletes the sibling provider_id control from the edit form in the same diff. P'(b)'s dual-leg requirement (persisted delta + fresh-session user surface) has no second leg to stand on for the feature's own primary claim, because the product itself never re-exposes the value through any front door.
breaks.fix: Either (a) accept that this claim class is structurally CND-only and document it as a legitimate theory outcome rather than a gap to force-fix, or (b) widen 'fresh-session user surface' to explicitly allow a read-only admin API GET the dashboard doesn't currently render, if the harness is allowed to treat 'the value is retrievable via the same authenticated session's read surface, even if no widget shows it' as satisfying (b). That is a real policy decision the theory should make explicit, not paper over.

breaks.detail: The one indirect behavioral leg available (customer checkout success/failure via validateFulfillmentData) is not discriminating in the only CONJURE-able environment: the built-in 'manual' provider's validateFulfillmentData is a no-op passthrough (`return data`) and validateOption always returns true. A WORKS verdict built on 'checkout succeeded' would be a false WORKS — checkout succeeds regardless of whether the FO data is correct, garbage, or (pre-PR) absent. This is a new false-WORKS vector not on the known list: the feature's only real discriminating power lives in third-party fulfillment provider plugins (Shopify, ShipStation, etc.) not part of the CONJURE-able topology, so any sandbox using the shipped default provider structurally cannot exercise the feature's true validation semantics.
breaks.fix: Either seal this specific effect class into CND-by-policy whenever the resolved provider's validator is a known no-op (requires the harness to introspect which provider is bound and flag non-discriminating validators before compiling the promise), or require a real non-trivial validator provider to be part of the declared environment for this feature (raising it from CONJURE to something closer to ATTACH/BYO), and refuse to compile a WORKS-eligible claim otherwise.

breaks.detail: Exercising the downstream checkout path (add-shipping-method-to-cart / list-shipping-options-for-cart) front-door-only requires a fully wired region -> stock_location -> fulfillment_set -> service_zone -> shipping_option -> sales_channel -> cart chain. All of it is creatable via the real admin UI (no fixture shortcuts needed), but it is a long, multi-screen setup sequence before the single discriminating click. This doesn't break the theory, but is a real cost multiplier on 'medium' size-class PRs whose true effect sits several hops downstream of the changed files.
breaks.fix: None needed structurally; note as a practical cost driver for scoping k/N repro budgets on similarly deep commerce PRs.

sonnetDifficulty: Moderately hard for me in two specific ways: (1) recognizing that the edit-form deletion (provider_id block removed) wasn't cosmetic but eliminated the only other place this data could be re-observed took a careful side-by-side diff read, not a skim; a shallower pass would have assumed 'edit form still lets you view/change provider' and wrongly declared a dual-leg WORKS achievable. (2) The trivial-validator-masking finding required fetching and reading the actual manual-fulfillment.ts source rather than assuming from the diff alone — the diff itself gives zero signal that validateFulfillmentData is a no-op; without pulling that file I could easily have proposed 'checkout succeeds' as a valid second leg and produced a false WORKS prediction. Both are exactly the kind of 'genius-dependence' the theory needs to survive without: a lower-effort agent skimming only the PR diff (not the wider repo) would very plausibly have compiled a false-positive-prone promise here.
newVectors: FW-16 (new): asymmetric CRUD surface — a create-time-only field with no read/edit-time UI rendering forces the dual-leg check to have no legitimate second leg, independent of egress/third-party concerns (distinct from the known FW list, which assumes the value is at least readable somewhere in the app).

FW-17 (new): trivial-validator masking — when a feature's real discriminating power is enforced by a pluggable component (here, a fulfillment provider's validateFulfillmentData) and the only CONJURE-able instance of that component is a no-op stub, any behavioral effect check routed through it degenerates to a vacuous pass; sharper and more mechanically identifiable than the general FW-14 (sandbox config != prod config) because it doesn't need a config mismatch to bite — the stock/default implementation itself is non-discriminating by design (it's a local-dev placeholder).
conjureFeasibility: Real for the topology itself: medusa's admin dashboard + API + Postgres can be conjured from repo (yarn dev, migrations, seed). Real for the create-time claim's persisted-state leg. Sealed-out/CND for the dual-leg confirmation of the same claim (no UI leg exists anywhere in the app). Doubled-to-vacuous for the downstream behavioral leg via the only conjure-able ('manual') fulfillment provider, since its validator is a passthrough — using it forces CND rather than letting it stand in as a legitimate WORKS witness.
openQuestions: Does the harness's definition of 'fresh-session user surface' in P'(b) permit a raw authenticated GET the UI itself never renders, or must the value be visible in an actual rendered widget? This PR is a clean test case forcing that policy to be made explicit rather than left implicit.

Should a claim be allowed to compile at all when the only CONJURE-able implementation of a pluggable validation point is a known no-op — should the harness maintain a registry of 'known non-discriminating stock providers' and refuse WORKS-eligibility for effect checks routed through them?

Is there any first-party fulfillment provider plugin in the medusa ecosystem (outside packages/modules/providers/) with a non-trivial validateFulfillmentData that could legitimately serve as the environment's fulfillment provider for this PR's verification, without crossing into ATTACH/BYO territory?
compiledPromise: Discriminating claim: "When an admin, using only the admin dashboard UI, creates a new shipping option for a given fulfillment provider and selects one of that provider's Fulfillment Options (filtered by is_return matching the option type), the system persists a ShippingOption row whose `data` field equals that selected fulfillment option object — observed as a write-set delta on the `shipping_option` table bound to the create-action window." Negative: "An admin who opens the same create form and attempts to submit without selecting a Fulfillment Option is blocked client-side (zod fulfillment_option_id min(1) failure) and produces zero `shipping_option` writes — confirmed by an idle-baseline-matching harness diff showing no delta for that window." Both claims are in-scope, non-quantified (no any/all/every), and structurally sound; the blocker is not the claim's clarity but P'(b)'s dual-leg mechanics finding no legitimate second leg for the positive claim in a stock CONJURE sandbox.
